summary.intent: Plan and fully execute phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation ECIES unwrap consolidation), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and creating a PR.
summary.outcome: Planning completed successfully with 5 plans across 3 waves covering 6 requirements (scope expanded mid-session to include batch and drag-and-drop move). Wave 1 (SDK op + useFolderNavigation refactor) was fully executed; Wave 2 (web single-item move) was dispatched but the session transcript ends before its result is confirmed.

repo: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is fully key-agnostic (takes raw key bytes, no owner/recipient distinction) — reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case
share_keys entries are keyed by itemId (file UUID), not parent folder — file keys do NOT need re-registration after an intra-share move
adoptSharedFolderResult must be called only once for the source result; calling it for the dest would corrupt the sharedFolderTree projection
sdkCore.moveItem throws on name collision ('An item with this name already exists in destination') — no auto-rename logic needed
@internal on ensureFolderLoaded is documentation-only (CipherBoxClient is already exported); call it directly from the web layer without a new public alias
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) must have moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree explicitly added
File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns', NOT FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted (owner-wrapped; recipient cannot decrypt it)
Batch move is a web-layer pattern only — loops single-item client.moveItem (useFileBrowserActions → handleBatchMoveConfirm → useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems); no dedicated SDK batch method exists
Drag-and-drop move lives in FileListItem (handleDragStart is multi-select-aware → drop target on folder rows → handleDropOnFolder)

workflow: Sequential plan execution (no parallel worktrees) is safer for autonomous/AFK runs — the parallel worktree merge-back protocol is error-prone to hand-drive and concurrent test runs can starve RAM

After adding new public methods to the SDK package, the SDK dist must be rebuilt before web packages can typecheck against them — index.d.ts is a barrel re-export, actual declarations are in client.d.ts
